// expr: the full expression grammar - precedence, parentheses,
// unary operators, short-circuit logic and constant folding.
n := 7;
total := n*3 + 1;
assert.Equal(tb, "22", fmt.Sprintf("%d", total));

grouped := (n + 3) * 2;
assert.Equal(tb, "20", fmt.Sprintf("%d", grouped));

neg := -n + 2;
assert.Equal(tb, "-5", fmt.Sprintf("%d", neg));

inv := ^n;
assert.Equal(tb, "-8", fmt.Sprintf("%d", inv));

half := n / 2;
rem := n % 2;
assert.Equal(tb, "3 1", fmt.Sprintf("%d %d", half, rem));

bits := n&3 | 8;
assert.Equal(tb, "11", fmt.Sprintf("%d", bits));

sh := n << 2 >> 1;
assert.Equal(tb, "14", fmt.Sprintf("%d", sh));

// The right side of && only runs when the left does not decide, so
// the division by zero never happens.
zero := 0;
ok := n > 5 && n+1 <= 8;
assert.True(tb, ok);
safe := zero != 0 && 7/zero > 1;
assert.Equal(tb, false, safe);
no := !ok || safe;
assert.Equal(tb, false, no);

// An all-constant tree folds at compile time.
day := 60 * 60 * 24;
assert.Equal(tb, "86400", fmt.Sprintf("%d", day));

// Arithmetic wraps at the type's width, as compiled Go does.
var w uint8;
w = 200;
wide := w*2 + 1;
assert.Equal(tb, "145", fmt.Sprintf("%d", wide));

f := 1.5;
scaled := (f + 0.5) * 2.0;
assert.Equal(tb, "4", fmt.Sprintf("%v", scaled));

s := "go";
msg := s + "-" + s;
assert.Equal(tb, "go-go", msg);
within := msg >= "go" && msg < "gp";
assert.True(tb, within);
